title: Redaction is deterministic and rule-based; no model, no network
context: The subscription-only-LLM estate rule and the requirement that redaction be testable both point away from model-assisted redaction. Every replacement must be defensible under review; every ledger row must be reproducible from the inputs.
decision: src/feedback/redact.js applies the eight rules of design section 5 (project root, other absolute paths, emails, non-allowlisted hosts, private IPs, secret-looking strings, operator identity, size and shape). The vendor host allowlist ships as src/feedback/redact-allowlist.json and is extended per project via rcf/feedback-settings.json:redaction.allowHosts[]. A body that still matches rule 5 on the second pass is refused, not sent.
consequences: Redaction is testable with a fixture corpus and deterministic under review. Some over-redaction is expected (a benign name matching an entropy rule); the disclosure ledger surfaces every case so the operator can see and the agent can rewrite. The rendered output is what leaves; the stored raw entry is untouched.

alternativesConsidered.name: Model-assisted redaction or summarisation
alternativesConsidered.summary: Route the body through a model to strip PII and produce a compact narrative.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Estate subscription-only rule and non-deterministic output that cannot be unit-tested.
